newsitem.title: UK: FINNISH, IRISH EMU EXPECTATIONS RISE - JP MORGAN.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH, IRISH EMU EXPECTATIONS RISE - JP MORGAN.

text.p: Market expectations that a broad group of countries will launch the planned single European currency in 1999 pushed higher again in the past week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed on Friday.

The chances of Finland and Ireland joining Germany in European economic and monetary union rose by eight percentage points to 79 percent and 77 percent respectively, according to JP Morgan's "EMU calculator." The calculator is derived from the interest-rate swaps market.
Irish hopes of founding EMU have leapt in the past month, climbing 27 points from 50 percent on July 11.

The chances of Italy and Spain joining their ranks were little changed in the latest week but remained more than 75 percent. The probability of France and Belgium founding EMU was unchanged from last week at 100 percent.

Britain is still viewed as the least likely country to join EMU at its start, but its perceived probability of membership has risen to 33 percent from 25 percent a week ago and 17 percent four weeks ago.
JP Morgan said there was a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
